text: Nora and her grandpa went fishing at dawn. The lake was still and gray. Grandpa showed her how to hold the rod and wait. Nora was not good at waiting. She wanted to talk and move. But then the line pulled, and she held on tight. Together they brought in a small silver fish. Nora looked at it, and then she put it back in the water. Grandpa smiled. "Patience and kindness," he said. "You have both."

The new kid at school sat alone at lunch. His name was Omar, and he did not speak much English yet. Ella saw him and took her tray to his table. She pointed to her apple and said, "Apple." Omar smiled and said a word in his language. They traded words all through lunch. By the end of the week, they had a list of fifty words and a new friendship.

Pip was a tiny robot who cleaned the floors of a big library. Every night, Pip rolled between the shelves and picked up dust. One night, Pip found a book on the floor. It was open to a picture of the sea. Pip had never seen the sea. After that, Pip read one page every night. Soon Pip knew about whales, ships and storms, and loved the library more than ever.

On the hill above the village stood an old windmill. The children said it was haunted because it creaked at night. Kai was brave and climbed up to see. Inside, he found a family of owls living in the top. The creaking was just the wind and the old wood. Kai told the others, and from then on they came to watch the owls fly out at sunset.

Lena wanted to win the school race more than anything. She practiced every morning. On race day, her friend Ruby fell near the end. Lena stopped and helped her up. They crossed the line together, last of all. Lena was sad for a moment. Then the whole school cheered for them. The teacher said that was the best finish of the day.

Every winter, the old baker on Elm Street left bread on the steps for anyone who was hungry. No one knew why. One cold night, a boy named Felix waited to see him. The baker told Felix that once, long ago, someone had done the same for him. Felix never forgot it. Years later, Felix had a bakery of his own, and bread on the steps every winter.
